notes: This is the row the entity check exists for, and it is the most useful finding even though the product cannot be bought. The shop is iHostART, run from Orastie, Romania. Its company is MAN HOSTING GMB H S.R.L., CUI 44507600, incorporated 29 June 2021, registered at Str. Tudor Vladimirescu nr. 60, Orastie - the same address a third-party profile gives for the shop. Three independent Romanian company-data sources, read today, agree that its 2025 turnover was 0 RON, down 100 percent from 150,075 RON in 2024, and that it reported 0 employees. The company is not dissolved and carries no ANAF debt, so this is not the dissolved-UK-company trap; it is the quieter one: an entity that is still registered, still lists products, and reported no revenue at all in its last filed year. A buyer sending EUR 5.40 or any other sum to it is buying from a shell whose filings say nothing came in last year. On top of that the products cannot be bought: all three in the group read '0 Available' and the product route answers 'Out of Stock'. And no price renders on any route tried - the only figure anywhere is EUR 5.40 a year from a September 2022 forum post by the operator, which is four years old and is recorded as reported, not as the current price. The specification itself is worth noting's purposes: the NAT64 plan opens zero ports on its shared IPv4 and gives a /64, so it is IPv6-only in practice, which is exactly the shape is hunting. What is not established: the current price, the checkout fields, and whether the shop and the company are still the same operator today - the profile claim dates from 2022. A buyer who wants this should ask for a current invoice before paying anything.
